sample_unit: anonymized soft tissue sarcoma cases (each queried 21 times per model)

links.outcome: Intra-model and inter-model consistency of LLM treatment recommendations across repeated queries
links.effect: High inter-model and intra-model consistency in only 20% of cases; alignment with human consensus in only 20-60% of cases.
links.quote: LLMs demonstrated high inter-model and intra-model consistency in only 20% of cases, and their recommendations aligned with human consensus in only 20-60% of cases.

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM sarcoma treatment recommendations with guideline-based expert MTB recommendations and harmful alternatives
links.effect: Common human recommendations often absent in LLM outputs; best model (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) aligned with experts in only 60% of cases; potentially harmful alternative recommendations observed.
links.quote: Discrepancies were particularly notable, where common human recommendations were often absent in LLM outputs.

links.outcome: Proportion of LLM responses whose cited sources were clearly derived from German S3 sarcoma guidelines
links.effect: Sources clearly derived from the German S3 sarcoma guidelines in only 24.8% to 55.2% of responses.
links.quote: Additionally, the sources for the recommendation rationale of LLMs were clearly derived from the German S3 sarcoma guidelines in only 24.8% to 55.2% of the responses.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to prepare for multidisciplinary tumor board discussions
Referral of complex sarcoma cases to high-volume sarcoma centers

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance, consistency, and safety of several LLMs against multidisciplinary tumor board recommendations for soft tissue sarcoma cases without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
